analysis:
Examined both documentation changes, full supplied base/head surroundings for cluster-always-on.md, and two-mac-cluster.md's patch and metadata. The documents replace manual-only cluster updates with coordinated staging, peer-progress checks, bounded non-cancelling drains, commit/restart and candidate recovery. No independently supported security regression follows from documentation alone; the referenced implementations are not supplied.

Integration should verify docs/provider/cluster-always-on.md:117-162 against ClusterServiceCommand.swift, ClusterPairUpdateCycle.swift and ClusterPairUpdate.swift: update-disable gates, authenticated peer progress bound to the same release/cycle, stale-progress handling, admission reopening and the worker-free fallback's install-time fence. These affect TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, A-018 and T-010. Compare two-mac-cluster.md's changed manual-update description (head:569-578) with actual CLI ordering: it says installation precedes the service's coordinated drain, whereas automatic updates commit only after both drained.

Candidate recovery at cluster-always-on.md:164-181 explicitly lacks a surviving rollback process and cannot recover a supervisor that fails after passing --version but before starting its service. Review ClusterCandidateRecovery and supervisor/launchd integration against T-043; this documented limitation is not proof of a newly exploitable implementation defect. Verify predecessor integrity/quarantine and fresh-heartbeat promotion, plus same-worker-build replanning and current release authorization at :183-186 (A-011, A-016, A-017, T-053, T-054). Neither --version nor equal worker builds establish serving qualification. No supplied change alters plaintext handling, encryption, key custody, cache isolation, billing or privileged-helper permissions. Missing implementation coverage remains material to the new update lifecycle.
